title: CISA Warns Oracle HTTP Server Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Access and Modify Critical Data
content_md: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a critical Oracle HTTP Server vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog after confirming evidence of active exploitation. Tracked as CVE-2026-21962, the flaw affects Oracle HTTP Server and the Oracle WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in. CISA described it as an improper access control issue that can allow unauthenticated attackers to access and modify critical data without valid credentials. The addition was announced on August 24, 2026, placing the vulnerability among the security flaws that federal agencies must prioritize under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04. CISA Warns Oracle HTTP Server Flaw Oracle HTTP Server is widely deployed as a web-tier component in enterprise environments, often fronting Oracle WebLogic Server applications and business-critical services. A weakness in the proxy plug-in layer can therefore create a pathway for attackers to interact with backend applications or data stores that administrators may believe are shielded from direct internet access. CVE-2026-21962 is particularly concerning because exploitation does not require authentication. Attackers able to reach a vulnerable endpoint may be able to bypass intended access restrictions, retrieve sensitive information, or alter data handled by affected systems.
